Saved. The skill now has a dedicated H-Spread/IQR section.

Summary of what was generalizable here:

The miss (57.53 vs 57.50, off by exactly 0.03) was a rounding-STAGE error, not a data error. The question said "use the intermediate values rounded to the tenths of billions before computing the H spread." I rounded the wrong stage — the correct reading is that "intermediate values" = the two quartiles Q1 and Q3, which get rounded to tenths and THEN subtracted. That makes the H-spread land on a clean tenth (57.50). I instead rounded something else (the input data), let Type-7 interpolation re-introduce hundredths, and got a non-tenth 57.53.

Key generalizable rule now in the skill: when an instruction says "round intermediate values to X before computing," the "intermediate values" are the immediate inputs to the FINAL operation (here Q1/Q3), not the raw table data. Diagnostic: if the answer isn't a clean tenth when the rule demanded tenth-rounded intermediates, you rounded the wrong stage. Also captured: H Spread = IQR = Q3-Q1 via Type-7 (numpy default), and FY = Oct–Sep, not calendar months.

No memory update needed — the memory file is near its char cap and this nuance is better placed in the skill where the full IQR procedure lives.
